properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 8 at 7:45PM MST until August 8 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 745 PM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located near Black Canyon
City, or 35 miles southwest of Camp Verde, moving southwest at 20
mph.

HAZARD...Quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Damage to vehicles is expected.

Locations impacted include...
Black Canyon City, Agua Fria National Monument, Sunset Point Rest
Area, Rock Springs and Bumble Bee.

This includes Interstate 17 between mile markers 242 and 255.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Black Canyon Campground.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing large hail.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued August 8 at 10:43PM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
At 1043 PM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Pleasantville, or 7 miles west of Somerset, moving east at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
New Lexington, Somerset, Perry State Forest, Thornport, Harbor Hills,
Crooksville, Thornville, Junction City, and Glenford.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued August 8 at 9:29PM CDT by NWS Dodge City KS
properties.description:
At 928 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 8
miles northwest of Wilburton. This thunderstorm was nearly
stationary.

localized reduced visibilities and lightning induced

unsecured objects.

Stevens Counties.
properties.instruction:

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued August 8 at 7:23PM MST until August 8 at 9:45PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Gila County in east central Arizona...

* Until 945 PM MST.

* At 723 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms produced heavy
rain across the warned area earlier today. Between 1.75 and 3
inches of rain have fallen. Flooding impacts will continue, but no
additional rainfall is expected. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Young and Pendleton Mesa.

This includes State Route 288 between mile markers 294 and 311.
properties.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued August 8 at 9:19PM CDT until August 8 at 11:00PM CDT by NWS Nashville TN

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Spring Hill, Nolensville and Thompson's Station.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued August 8 at 6:44PM PDT until August 8 at 9:45PM PDT by NWS Reno NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Mono County in northern California...

* WHEN...Until 945 PM PDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 640 PM PDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen.
- While thunderstorms producing heavy rain have ended, lingering
localized flooding may continue going into the evening.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Twin Lakes, Robinson Creek Campground and Trumbull Lake
Campground.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued August 8 at 9:27PM EDT until August 9 at 12:30AM EDT by NWS State College PA
properties.description:
FFWCTP

The National Weather Service in State College has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southern Warren County in north central Pennsylvania...

* Until 1230 AM EDT.

* At 927 PM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 2
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3
inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sheffield, Garland, Grand Valley and Tidioute.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

In hilly terrain, hundreds of low water crossings are potentially
dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded roads. Find
an alternate route.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 8 at 8:13PM CDT until August 9 at 3:35PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding occurs, and causes
sloughs and peripheral channels near the main stream to cut off
areas of the flood plain, isolating livestock and damaging
equipment in low areas. Oil field tank batteries and pump jacks
flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 14.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tonight and fall below action stage by late Monday.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 14.3
feet on 05/24/2004.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.
